title: Orchestrated evacuation simulation — cross-region failover exercise notes
content:
Summary:
This doc captures notes from the Orchestrated Evacuation Simulation executed on 2025-01-15 targeting a controlled region-level power/network evacuation for us-east-1. The drill exercised multi-region routing, DNS TTL adjustments, warm-standby promotion, KV cache preseed and live traffic-weight shifting. Objective: validate playbooks, identify race conditions in routing/fallback logic, and surface observability gaps.

High-level outcome:
- Drill succeeded in preserving API availability (95th p50 token latency maintained under SLO for traffic that reached healthy regions).
- Two operational issues identified that require runbook updates: a DNS propagation timing mismatch and an edge LB healthcheck flapping behavior during weight reconfiguration.

Pre-sim setup (what we did before traffic movement):
- Announced maintenance in #sre-ops and to oncall for hosted-api and dedicated teams.
- Reduced dns TTL for service.example.api from 300 to 30s at T-48h and verified via dig from 5 regions.
- Pre-warmed KV cache on warm-standby in eu-west-1 for top 50 prefixes (script: infra/scripts/preseed-kv.sh PR#876).
- Marked warm-standby pools with staged routing policy (priority: primary(us-east-1) > warm-standby(eu-west-1) > fallback(us-central-1)).
- Ran dry-run of weight-change plan in staging to ensure automation runbook applied correct LB config.

Timeline (concise):
- 2025-01-15 09:00 UTC: Kickoff, confirm participants (Aisha, Ben, Lina, Marco, Priya, oncall).
- 09:10 UTC: Orchestration started — BGP announcements toggled to simulate region network loss (control-plane change, not full outage).
- 09:12 UTC: Automated routing policy detected region degradation and started traffic diversion to warm-standby with gradual 5% increments per 30s.
- 09:13 UTC: Observed spike in 1m error-rate in edge LBs (healthcheck failures).
- 09:14 UTC: Two edge LB instances flapped; automation paused at 30% diversion as safety cutoff. Manual intervention initiated.
- 09:18 UTC: Investigated LB logs — a config race where new weight + health-checking caused backend pool to be temporarily mis-evaluated. Reapplied stable config; LB recovered at 09:21.
- 09:24 UTC: Resumed diversion at smaller step increments (2% per 20s) to complete migration by 09:36.
- 09:40 UTC: Verified traffic fully routed to warm-standby and fallback regions. KV cache hit-rate for preseeded prefixes: 72% during first 5 minutes, stabilizing to >88% at 10 minutes.
- 10:00 UTC: Completed after-action notes and initial triage.

Failures and root-cause hypotheses:
1) LB healthcheck flapping during weight reconfiguration:
   - Observation: two edge LB instances reported failing healthchecks immediately after weight updates; metrics show synthetic health probes returning transient 502s during the LB reconfiguration window.
   - Hypothesis: our LB control plane applies weight updates and healthcheck recalculations in separate transactions; intermediate state triggers aggressive healthcheck timeouts.
   - Impact: automation paused at safety cutoff; required manual step to stabilize.

2) DNS propagation timing mismatch with client resolver behaviors:
   - Observation: despite TTL lowered to 30s, ~2% of test clients continued to send traffic to the evacuated region for up to 7 minutes.
   - Hypothesis: some corporate resolvers ignore low TTLs or have negative caching; also mobile carrier resolvers (APAC) showed longer caching.
   - Impact: small residual traffic caused additional load on half-evacuated region for a short period; KV cache miss rate was higher there.

Positive signals:
- KV cache preseed reduced cold-start miss tail substantially; median token-latency improvement for warmed prefixes was ~18% vs non-warmed.
- Gradual diversion automation handled rollbacks cleanly when pause triggered.
- Observability pipelines (traces/metrics) captured cross-region tracing IDs allowing us to correlate errors to routing changes.

Immediate mitigations applied during drill:
- Paused automation and rolled back weight change to prior stable config when LB flap detected (manual escalation to LB owners).
- Increased probe timeout for the edge LB pool temporarily to avoid transient failover while reconfiguring weights. Documented exact CLI commands used.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- SRE: Add atomic LB reconfigure recipe to automation so weight updates and healthcheck recalculation are applied in a single transaction where supported (owner: Ben Gomez, ETA: 2025-02-06).
- Infrastructure: Implement a canary pattern for LB weight changes that exercises single-instance updates before cluster-wide change (owner: Marco Alvarez, ETA: 2025-03-01).
- DNS/Platform: Add a pre-check list for resolver behavior by geolocation and escalate if non-compliant resolvers are detected (owner: Lina Zhou, ETA: 2025-02-10).
- Product/Docs: Update evacuation runbook with explicit TTL change cadence and note unexpected resolver behavior; include fallback plan if residual traffic >5% after 10 minutes (owner: Priya Menon, ETA: 2025-01-30).
- Observability: Add a dedicated dashboard panel that shows "residual region traffic percent" and KV-cache preseed hit-rate by prefix during a failover (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2025-02-14).

Runbook changes to propose (text to add):
- Pre-sim checklist: verify TTL change effect from 3 distinct public resolvers (Google, Cloudflare, ISP test node) and run traceroutes from 5 sample client ASNs.
- Weight change algorithm: default to smaller steps (2%) and step cooldown of 20s when switching to warm-standby for first 10% to reduce LB reconfiguration churn.
- LB healthcheck safe-mode: when automation detects >1 instance healthcheck flap within 60s of a weight change, revert to previous weights and call out to LB owners immediately.
- KV cache preseed guidance: always preseed top-N prefixes covering 80% of traffic by token-count for target region; log prefix preseed success and hit-rate in infra logs.

Observability gaps and recommended improvements:
- Missing synthetic probe variety: we currently lack probes that mimic small-batch, low-qps clients; add a probe mode that simulates realistic small sessions during diversion.
- Tracing continuity: about 4% of traces lost region metadata during the BGP-control-plane toggle; need a lightweight middleware shim that stamps region-handling info before router-level handoffs.

Misc notes and friction points encountered:
- Control-plane tooling (internal CLI) UI warns but doesn't block conflicting LB operations; add a warning with a locking mechanism for rollout operations.
- Communication cadence: oncall L2 felt the initial automation pause message was ambiguous. Proposed to standardize an "automation pause" template with required immediate information (reason, observed metric, safe revert command).

Post-sim risk classification (quick):
- High: LB atomicity (customer-impact if left unaddressed)
- Medium: DNS residual traffic from stubborn resolvers
- Low: KV cache preseed coverage gaps for long-tail prefixes

Follow-ups (meeting schedule):
- 2025-01-20 16:00 UTC: Deep-dive with LB owners and infra (Ben, Marco) to design the atomic reconfigure change.
- 2025-01-22 09:00 UTC: DNS resolver behavior survey results (Lina to present).
- 2025-02-03 15:00 UTC: Runbook review and sign-off (all owners).

Appendix: commands/artefacts used during the drill:
- preseed script: infra/scripts/preseed-kv.sh --prefix-file top50-prefixes.txt --region eu-west-1 (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/876)
- LB rollback CLI (internal): redwood-lb set-weights --pool service-edge --weights-file weights-stable.json --force-atomic
- DNS change: dnsctl set-ttl service.example.api 30 --apply-id evc-sim-2025-01-15
- Observability queries: grafana query id "region_failover_overview" and traces filter tag="evac-sim-2025"

Notes to reviewers:
- This was a controlled simulation; we did not disable production infrastructure beyond BGP announcement toggles that mimic network failure.
- Please call out any missed teardown steps or missing telemetry which would have helped diagnosis during the 09:12-09:21 window.

End of notes.
